newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan steps up efforts to reduce hog crisis.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan steps up efforts to reduce hog crisis.

text.p: Taiwan intensified its efforts to save its hog industry on Wednesday, with lawmakers urging the government to restore consumers' confidence in pork products and officials holding talks with Japan on easing an import ban.

An outbreak of hog foot-and-mouth disease on March 20 has prompted a total ban on pork exports and an eradication campaign that has battered the stock market and dealt a blow to Taiwan's gathering economic recovery.
Wellcome Taiwan Company, one of the island's biggest supermarket chains, said pork sales were down 30 to 40 percent since the announcement of the outbreak.
Vivian Lin, a spokeswoman for Wellcome, said chicken sales had risen by more than 20 percent as pork demand had declined.
Lin said Wellcome and other supermarkets required their pork suppliers to provide safety guarantees in an attempt to win back customers' confidence.
The Taiwan government is trying to reduce export losses as a result of a ban on Taiwan pork by Japan, the biggest buyer.
An economic ministry statement said Japan had agreed to allow entry of 13,000 tonnes of frozen pork already in Japanese ports.
Talks were under way to allow shipment to Japan of 40,000 tonnes of Taiwan pork that was slaughtered and frozen before Taiwan's March 20 announcement of the disease outbreak, officials said.
But a Japan's Agriculture Ministry official denied that Tokyo would allow entry of any Taiwan pork already in Japanese ports.
In a bid to rescue the hog industry, the ruling Nationalist Party said it would ask all its officials to eat pork in their lunch boxes and serve pork dishes at government banquets.
"As long as an official uses the taxpayers' money, the meal he eats has to include at least two pork dishes," said Hung Shing-jung, a Nationalist lawmaker and spokesman.
Taiwan has pooled billion-dollar funds in the war against the hog epidemic to finance the massive slaughter and vaccination.
Taiwan officials have said the export value of Taiwan's hog industry in 1996 stood at T$43.6 billion (US$1.55 billion).
Taiwan economists have warned the hog industry crisis combined with the impact on the subsequent feed and food processors could cost the island up to one percent of its Gross Domestic Product.
The council ordered the slaughter of all hogs, even healthy ones, at affected farms to eradicate the disease and said this meant over one million hogs would be destroyed.
Officials said Taiwan's fast-moving hog foot and mouth epidemic had spread to 716 pig breeding centres by late on Wednesday -- double the 357 reported on Monday.

Experts backed by soldiers continued a mass slaughter of hogs plagued by the highly contagious disease, with agriculture officials reporting that over 666,000 diseased and healthy pigs at affected farms would have to be destroyed.
Taiwan plans to import eight million doses of vaccine to combat the outbreak. It had only 50,000 doses when the outbreak was confirmed.
